newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-DONG PUTS OLYMPIC TEARS BEHIND HIM.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-DONG PUTS OLYMPIC TEARS BEHIND HIM.

text.p: Tears shed in Atlanta were forgotten on Saturday as Dong Jiong, Olympic silver medallist, won the All England badminton men's singles final, brushing aside Chinese compatriot Sun Jun 15-9 15-5.
Dong, probably the most dynamic player on the men's circuit, had gained revenge late on Friday on Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen, who took Olympic gold last summer.

He overcame the tall Dane in straight games, a perfect prelude for Saturday's win over Sun Jun, who had claimed his place in the final with an excellent win over world champion Heryanto Arbi of Indonesia.
Truth to tell, however, the final was a lacklustre affair.
Dong was largely in control and the only time Sun, a former world junior champion, got within striking distance, he ruined his chance with errors at the net.
It was 23-year-old Dong's first major success and on current form the world championship in Glasgow in May looks well within his grasp.

Saturday looked like being a memorable day for the Chinese. Top seeds Ge Fei and Gu Jun retained their women's doubles title with a 15-6 15-9 victory over second seeded Eliza and Resiana Zelin of Indonesia.

Later, in the women's singles final, world champion Ye Zhaoying was due to meet Chinese compatriot Gong Zhichao and the mixed doubles could also fall the Chinese way, courtesy of Ge and Liu Yong, the joint fifth seeds.
